title: High-NA EUV lithography
summary: The next lithography generation, with larger optics and finer resolution.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

High-numerical-aperture EUV scanners use larger mirrors and a different optical path to print finer features, and cost well over €300m per tool. ASML shipped early systems to research and logic customers, with imec's pilot line providing a neutral testbed. Adoption depends on whether chipmakers can justify the cost against multi-patterning on existing EUV tools.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Early commercial
Estimated window 2024–2030
Confidence label Confident
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

Each lithography generation concentrates power in one supplier, which makes export-control policy a first-order variable.

What Would Change The View

  • Tool shipments and availability.
  • Cost per wafer versus multi-patterning.
  • Export licensing for China.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
